name: CONTEXTUAL
description: A dataset for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models. Contains 506 human-crafted instructions requiring joint reasoning over textual and visual elements in images across 8 real-world scenarios: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes.

citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., & Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources: LAION-5B (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract categories using keyword search with CLIP-retrieval UI), Rico Dataset (for Application Usage category with 66,000 UI screens from 9,300 Android apps), Open WebText Initiative website screenshots (for Web Usage category), and existing VQA datasets including InfographicVQA (for Infographic category) and STVQA/ESTVQA (for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes category). Human annotators then created instruction-response pairs for selected images following specific guidelines requiring context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B dataset (using CLIP-retrieval UI with category-specific keywords), Rico Dataset (66,000 UI screens from 9,300 Android apps), Open WebText Initiative (website screenshots), InfographicVQA test set, STVQA test set, and ESTVQA test set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Stage 1: Images categorized under Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract underwent manual filtering to guarantee suitability for annotation. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, heuristic-based filtering was performed using PaddleOCR to detect text in images, selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of words. Stage 2: Authors divided into two groups annotated four categories each following strict annotation guidelines. Stage 3: MTurk workers verified correctness of each sample, with 96% found to be correctly annotated. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and each author group reviewed samples created by the other group to ensure adherence to guidelines and filter low-quality samples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human annotators (authors divided into two groups) created instruction-response pairs following specific guidelines: (a) instructions must require context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements, avoiding instructions answerable by text-based reasoning over OCR alone; (b) diverse instructions including questions and imperative tasks; (c) varied complexity including extractive instructions and reasoning-based instructions. Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 - image shortlisting and filtering, Stage 2 - instruction-response pair annotation by author groups, Stage 3 - verification by MTurk workers (96% correctness rate) followed by cross-review by author groups.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for verification and human performance baseline)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified the correctness of each sample and found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Filtering out the incorrect samples, each author group reviewed the samples created by the other group to ensure adherence to guidelines and filtered out low-quality samples.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 (single human-written instruction and reference response per image)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Authors from University of California Los Angeles for instruction-response creation. MTurk workers (mainly from the US) for verification and human performance baseline evaluation.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4 model from PaddlePaddle library) for text detection during image filtering. ShareGPT-4V-7B for generating dense image captions in augmented LLM experiments.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples from the 506 will be released as validation set with reference responses, while reference responses for the remaining 406 samples will be kept hidden. The validation set maintains proportional representation of each category consistent with the overall benchmark (30 samples from Miscellaneous Natural Scenes and 10 samples from remaining categories).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables evaluation of multimodal models' capability for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning, which powers many real-world applications including interpreting text-rich scenes for assisting the visually impaired and creative understanding of abstract text-rich images like memes.
rai:dataBiases: Human annotators were mainly from the US, which may introduce linguistic diversity and writing style biases. The dataset authors acknowledge that the linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would change with different social groups. Human evaluation annotators were also primarily from the US, which may affect the reliability and generalizability of evaluation results across different regions and social groups.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging for modern LMMs with significant performance gaps: GPT-4V achieves 49.3% acceptance rating compared to 80.1% human baseline (30.8% gap). Models struggle particularly with time-related data and infographics. Open models lag significantly behind proprietary models. The dataset size (506 instances) may be limited for training purposes but is sufficient for evaluation with statistically significant results (P < 0.05 for model comparisons). Creating synthetic data for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning is challenging, as automatic dataset generation using OCR and image captions yields instructions solvable by OCR+LLM rather than requiring true context-sensitive reasoning.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large multimodal models' capabilities for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning. The dataset is designed for evaluation purposes to assess joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context in images. Usage includes: (1) benchmarking LMM performance across diverse visual scenarios, (2) fine-grained analysis of model capabilities across different visual contexts, (3) identifying gaps in model perception and reasoning abilities. Not recommended for training due to limited size (506 samples), though a synthetic data generation pipeline has been developed showing potential for scaling context-sensitive instructions.
